title: Thoracentesis (draining fluid from the chest)
what: Through a small puncture in your back or side, the doctor drains fluid that has built up around a lung. It is done with local numbing.
why: When fluid around a lung makes it hard to breathe, or when it needs to be tested to find the cause.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; fluid test results in a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change
If you have a strong cough
If you had this procedure before

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually your blood clotting is checked. The puncture spot is marked using ultrasound or an X-ray.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat as usual. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: During
prepare.text: It is important to sit still. If you feel a cough coming, warn the doctor.

bring: Your referral, images, and test results
steps: You sit, lean forward, and rest your arms on a table
The doctor chooses a spot on your back using ultrasound
The skin is cleaned and numbed with an injection
A thin needle goes in between the ribs
The fluid is slowly drained into a container
The needle is removed, and a bandage is put on
Sometimes a chest X-ray is done afterward
feel: A prick and stinging from the numbing
Near the end, you may cough or feel heaviness in your chest. Tell the doctor
after: You are usually watched for a while, and your breathing is checked
Keep the bandage on until the next day, unless your doctor says otherwise
red_flags: Shortness of breath that gets worse, chest pain, or coughing up blood: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) or redness at the puncture site: see a doctor right away

faq.a: The risk is small, since the spot is chosen with ultrasound. If it happens, it shows on an X-ray, and the doctor knows what to do.

faq.q: Why do I want to cough near the end?
faq.a: The lung expands as the fluid leaves. If the cough is strong, the procedure is stopped.

reminders.text: Chest fluid drainage today. Bring your images and a list of medicines. Keeping still during the procedure is important.
